messages:
kyle: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout we see ~12% drop in prefix KV cache hit-rate for ap-southeast. Started around 02:10 UTC. Digging in now.

maria: Ugh. Is that global or only ap-southeast?

kyle: Only ap-southeast. eu-west/na are steady. Query: `avg:prefix_cache.hitrate{region:ap-southeast}.rollup(avg,60)` shows decline from 72% -> 60% over 1h.

jen: @kyle any recent changes to keying or prompt normalization?

kyle: No prompt-normalization changes in runtime from our side. But I noticed PR 789 (client-prompt-normalize) merged yesterday morning. Might be related.

samir: FYI kernel selection change also introduced a different path for mid-length sequences that moves prefix handling into the quantized execution branch. That branch uses a slightly different KV key composition (context-length + prefix-hash vs old prefix-hash only).

maria: That would explain region-only hit drop if clients in ap-southeast are on newer SDK? Can we confirm SDK/agent versions by request logs?

kyle: Pulling traces... `http_logs.request_version{region:ap-southeast}.count()` shows a spike of agent v1.12.0 after the client deploy at 01:50 UTC. Others still mostly v1.11.x.

mike: So two orthogonal changes landed: client-side normalization + server kernel-selection that changed key composition. Combined they could produce a new key namespace and cold misses.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/engine-kernel-select completed at 01:45 UTC by @deploy-bot (canary -> stable).

jen: Do we have eviction/insert rates? If new keys are being inserted, cold miss + eviction churn could amplify.

kyle: Eviction spike on ap-southeast: `sum:prefix_cache.evictions{region:ap-southeast}.rollup(sum,60)` 3x baseline between 02:05-02:20 UTC. Insert rate also up.

samir: Profiling snapshot (short):
```
hot functions:
  copy_prefix_to_gpu 34ms -> 78ms (quant branch)
  compute_prefix_hash 2ms -> 2ms
  write_kv_store 12ms -> 18ms
```
copy_prefix_to_gpu increased due to extra packing in quantized path. Means longer write latency -> more time before caching completes -> more concurrent inserts -> pressure.

maria: Given this, mitigation options: 1) route ap-southeast traffic to eu-west for a short window, 2) use aliasing so old key lookup also checks new key shape, 3) revert kernel-select rollout, 4) roll back client change. Thoughts?

mike: Routing to eu-west is quick but increases latency for users. Might be acceptable for short window. Aliasing is safer long-term but needs code change to runtime key lookup (cheap). Revert might be fastest to restore hit-rate.

jen: Can we do a small server-side compatibility patch that checks both key shapes on lookup (fast path: check old key; if miss, check new key and promote)? That would be minimal and avoid broad rollback.

samir: I can whip up a compatibility lookup. Adds +1 lookup on miss — should be low cost because most will hit the first check. Plan: deploy compat canary to ap-southeast nodes only, measure hit-rate.

kyle: +1 to canary compat first. Also propose proactive warmup: backfill hot prefix keys from eu-west cache to ap-southeast once compat is live. A small fanout job can do that.

maria: Agree. Steps and timeline?

samir: Timeline: 1) Build compat lookup binary (15m). 2) Deploy canary to 10% of ap-southeast (20m). 3) If hit-rate improves >6pt in 10m window, ramp to 50% then 100%. 4) Kick warmup backfill job after 50%.

kyle: I'll prepare Datadog dashboard and alert for metric: `prefix_cache.hitrate{region:ap-southeast}` and `prefix_cache.evictions`. Also a latency SLO check for p95 generation.

jen: If canary fails, fall back to reversible actions: rollback kernel-select rollout (there's a rollback command) or route to eu-west.

mike: Command for rollback is: 
```
redwoodctl rollout rollback --deployment=engine-kernel-select --to=stable-01
```
Keep on-call ready.

infra-bot: ops-schedule-bot: On-call @maria for next 60m.

kyle: Starting compat build now. Will post canary shard list when ready.

maria: I'll open an incident ticket and add customers impacted.

samir: Compat branch pushed to `compat/kv-dual-lookup`. Building CI.

kyle: CI green, pushing canary to ap-southeast shard-3 (10% nodes). Rolling now.

jen: :eyes: monitoring...

kyle: Canary metrics after 7m: ap-southeast (canary nodes) hit-rate bumped from 61% -> 70%. Evictions decreased ~30%.

maria: Great! Any latency regressions from extra lookup?

samir: Measured add-on lookup cost is ~0.6ms on miss path. Hit path unchanged. No p95 impact visible.

kyle: I'll start backfill for top 2k prefixes from eu-west to ap-southeast. Backfill job id: bf-2026-03-18-01.

mike: After backfill and full rollout we should add an automated checker in our kernel-selection CI to validate key invariants (key-shape compatibility tests).

jen: Agreed. Also add a telemetry flag in canary to detect divergent keyspaces quickly.

kyle: Summary: compat canary looks good. Rolling to 100% now and running backfill. Will follow up in incident ticket with postmortem notes (root cause = simultaneous client normalization + server kernel key-shape change + regional rollout timing).

maria: Thanks all. Please @pager if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
